subject: horizontal stacked bar chart; order of variables, coord_flip()

messages.author: 30139ac7fefa3369
messages.subject: horizontal stacked bar chart; order of variables, coord_flip()
parts:
I've a data frame (mmt.ranking.sum_2, attached) with a list of 25 questions (1st column).
The questions are consecutively indexed: 9a-h, 10a-j, 11a-g as part of the question string.
For each question there are counts of answers in classes from 0-5 (2.-7. column), which should be stacked

aaa<-melt(mmt.ranking.sum_2[,1:7], id.vars="questions")
ggplot(aaa,aes(questions, value, fill=variable)) + geom_bar()+ coord_flip() + theme_bw()+ scale_fill_brewer()

In the original data frame & in the melted one the order of the questions is correct 9a-h, 10a-j, 11a-g.
But the order changes & reverses strangely in the final, horizontal chart: 9h-9a, 11g-11a, 10j-10a

This has already been answered here:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/17194798/ggplot-stacked-bar-chart-order-of-x-values-get-mixed-up

with
ggplot(aaa, aes(reorder(questions,as.numeric(gsub('([0-9]+).*','\\1', aaa$questions))) ,value, fill=variable))
+ geom_bar(stat='identity')
+ theme_bw()
+ coord_flip()
+ scale_fill_brewer()

The general order now is ok. 9a - 11g
But in the final (horizontal) chart they are listed bottom up instead of top down.

I have moved to this mailing list because I think this behaviour might be specifically caused by the coord_flip() funktion.
Any suggestions how to achieve a top-down vertical order 9a-11g?

Thanks
Georg

On Thu, Jun 20, 2013 at 3:31 AM, g.fritsch <g.fr...@boku.ac.at> wrote:
> I've a data frame (mmt.ranking.sum_2, attached) with a list of 25 questions
> (1st column).
> The questions are consecutively indexed: 9a-h, 10a-j, 11a-g as part of the
> question string.
> For each question there are counts of answers in classes from 0-5 (2.-7.
> column), which should be stacked
>
> aaa<-melt(mmt.ranking.sum_2[,1:7], id.vars="questions")
> ggplot(aaa,aes(questions, value, fill=variable)) + geom_bar()+ coord_flip()
> + theme_bw()+ scale_fill_brewer()
>
> In the original data frame & in the melted one the order of the questions is
> correct 9a-h, 10a-j, 11a-g.
> But the order changes & reverses strangely in the final, horizontal chart:
> 9h-9a, 11g-11a, 10j-10a

It's not strange if you understand the types of objects you're using.
My guess is that the questions variable is a factor, which by default
uses lexicographic ordering. You have to explicitly set the levels of
this factor variable to get the ordering you want. [BTW, this is one
reason why sending data sometimes is not sufficient; whether questions
is a character variable or a factor matters in this case. This is why
the output from the dput() function (whose argument is your R object
of interest) is more informative for potential helpers.]

>
> This has already been answered here:
> http://stackoverflow.com/questions/17194798/ggplot-stacked-bar-chart-order-of-x-values-get-mixed-up

>
> with
> ggplot(aaa, aes(reorder(questions,as.numeric(gsub('([0-9]+).*','\\1',
> aaa$questions))) ,value, fill=variable))
> + geom_bar(stat='identity')
> + theme_bw()
> + coord_flip()
> + scale_fill_brewer()
>
> The general order now is ok. 9a - 11g
> But in the final (horizontal) chart they are listed bottom up instead of top
> down.
>
> I have moved to this mailing list because I think this behaviour might be
> specifically caused by the coord_flip() funktion.
> Any suggestions how to achieve a top-down vertical order 9a-11g?

coord_flip() will take the minimum value on the original horizontal
axis and put it on top in the rotated graphic; if you think about it,
that's why the function is called coord_flip. The real problem is the
way that your questions are ordered as a factor. The following is not
especially elegant, but it shows how to define a factor in the aaa
data frame that will order the questions as you want.

# Extract out the question number and part
aaa$q1 <- vapply(aaa$questions,
function(x) unlist(strsplit(as.character(x), " "))[1],
character(1))
# Extract the unique question names
qlbl <- unique(as.character(aaa$questions))
# Define an ordering vector from 9a-11g
ord <- paste0(rep(9:11, c(8, 10, 7)), c(letters[1:8], letters[1:10],
letters[1:7]))
# Want reverse ordering and labels for the plot
aaa$q <- factor(aaa$q1, levels = rev(ord), labels = rev(qlbl))

ggplot(aaa, aes(x = q, y = value, fill = variable)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
theme_bw() +
labs(y = NULL) +
coord_flip() +
scale_fill_brewer()

If you want to rename the legend title, add fill = "<new-name>" to the
labs() statement.

Dennis
